title.zh: 卷五十二 列傳第四十六 止足
title.raw: 卷五十二 列傳第四十六 止足 Volume 52: The Self-Sufficient

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「亢之爲言也，知進而不知退，知存而不知亡。

translations.literal: The Changes says: "Excess means knowing advance but not retreat, knowing preservation but not loss.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says: "Excess" means knowing when to advance but not when to retreat, knowing how to preserve but not how to perish.

sentences.zh: 知進退存亡而不失其正者，其唯聖人乎！

translations.literal: Knowing advance, retreat, preservation, and loss without losing the Mean—surely only the sage can do this!"
translations.idiomatic: Only the sage knows advance, retreat, preservation, and loss without losing the Mean!"

sentences.zh: 」《傳》曰：「知足不辱，知止不殆。

translations.literal: The Tradition says: "Knowing sufficiency brings no disgrace; knowing when to stop brings no danger."
translations.idiomatic: The Tradition says: "Knowing sufficiency brings no disgrace; knowing when to stop brings no danger."

sentences.zh: 」然則不知夫進退，不達乎止足，殆辱之累，期月而至矣。

translations.literal: Yet if one does not understand advance and retreat, and does not grasp sufficiency and stopping, the burden of disgrace and danger arrives within a month.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those who misjudge advance and retreat and never grasp sufficiency and stopping invite disgrace and danger within a month.

sentences.zh: 古人之進也，以康世濟務也，以弘道厲俗也。

translations.literal: When men of old advanced, it was to bring peace to the age and aid affairs, to spread the Way and sharpen custom.
translations.idiomatic: Men of old advanced to comfort the age, aid affairs, spread the Way, and sharpen custom.

sentences.zh: 然其進也，光寵夷易，故愚夫之所乾沒；

translations.literal: When they advanced, glory and favor came easily, so fools scrambled for them;
translations.idiomatic: Advance brought easy glory and favor, so fools scrambled for them;

sentences.zh: 其退也，苦節艱貞，故庸曹之所忌憚。

translations.literal: when they withdrew, bitter integrity and hard constancy made vulgar men fear and resent them.
translations.idiomatic: withdrawal meant bitter integrity and hard constancy that vulgar men feared and resented.

sentences.zh: 雖禍敗危亡，陳乎耳目，而輕舉高蹈，寡乎前史。

translations.literal: Though disaster, defeat, peril, and ruin lay before their eyes, lightly to rise and walk high—few in earlier histories did so.
translations.idiomatic: Though disaster and ruin lay before their eyes, few in earlier histories lightly rose and walked away.

sentences.zh: 漢世張良功成身退，病臥卻粒，比於樂毅、范蠡至乎顛狽，斯爲優矣。

translations.literal: In Han, Zhang Liang achieved merit and withdrew his person, took to his bed and ceased grain—compared with Yue Yi and Fan Li, down to their ruin, he was the better case.
translations.idiomatic: In Han, Zhang Liang achieved merit and withdrew, took to his bed and ceased grain—compared with Yue Yi and Fan Li, even to their ruin, he was the better case.

sentences.zh: 其後薛廣德及二疏等，去就以禮，有可稱焉。

translations.literal: Afterward Xue Guangde and the two Shus and others withdrew and took office according to ritual—there is something to praise in that.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xue Guangde and the two Shus withdrew according to ritual—there is something to praise in that.

sentences.zh: 魚豢《魏略·知足傳》，方田、徐於管、胡，則其道本異。

translations.literal: Yu Huan's "Biography of Knowing Sufficiency" in the Wei Summary pairs Tian and Xu with Guan and Hu—their Ways were fundamentally different.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Huan's "Biography of Knowing Sufficiency" in the Wei Summary pairs Tian and Xu with Guan and Hu—their Ways were fundamentally different.

sentences.zh: 謝靈運《晉書·止足傳》，先論晉世文士之避亂者，殆非其人；

translations.literal: Xie Lingyun's "Biography of Knowing When to Stop" in the Jin History first discusses Jin-era literary men who fled disorder—hardly the right men;
translations.idiomatic: Xie Lingyun's Jin History "Biography of Knowing When to Stop" discusses literary men fleeing disorder—hardly the right men;

sentences.zh: 唯阮思曠遺榮好遁，遠殆辱矣。

translations.literal: only Ruan Sixiao left glory and loved withdrawal, far from nearly suffering disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: only Ruan Sixiao left glory and loved withdrawal, far from nearly suffering disgrace.

sentences.zh: 《宋書·止足傳》有羊欣、王微，咸其流亞。

translations.literal: The Song History "Biography of Knowing Sufficiency" has Yang Xin and Wang Wei—both of that stream.
translations.idiomatic: The Song History "Biography of Knowing Sufficiency" has Yang Xin and Wang Wei—both of that stream.

sentences.zh: 齊時沛國劉瓛，字子珪，辭祿懷道，棲遲養志，不戚戚於貧賤，不耽耽於富貴，儒行之高者也。

translations.literal: In Qi times Liu Huan of Pei, courtesy name Zigui, declined salary and cherished the Way, lingered and nourished his will—neither fretful in poverty nor greedy in wealth: a Confucian of the highest conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi, Liu Huan of Pei, styled Zigui, declined salary and cherished the Way, lingered to nourish his will—neither fretful in poverty nor greedy in wealth: a Confucian of the highest conduct.

sentences.zh: 梁有天下，小人道消，賢士大夫相招在位，其量力守志，則當世罔聞，時或有致事告老，或有寡志少欲，國史書之，亦以爲《止足傳》云。

translations.literal: When Liang possessed the realm, the way of petty men faded; worthy scholar-officials summoned one another to office. Those who measured their strength and kept their resolve went unmentioned in their day; sometimes men reported illness and retired, or had few desires— the state history records them in this "Biography of Knowing Sufficiency" as well.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang possessed the realm, petty ways faded and worthy men took office together. Those who measured strength and kept resolve went unmentioned; some reported illness and retired, some had few desires—the state history records them in this Biography of Knowing Sufficiency as well.

sentences.zh: 顧憲之

translations.literal: Gu Xianzhi
translations.idiomatic: Gu Xianzhi

sentences.zh: 顧憲之字士思，吳郡吳人也。

translations.literal: Gu Xianzhi, courtesy name Sisi, was a man of Wu in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Xianzhi, styled Sisi, came from Wu in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖抃之，宋鎮軍將軍、湘州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Bianzhi was Song General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Bianzhi was Song General Who Pacifies the Army and inspector of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 憲之未弱冠，州辟議曹從事，舉秀才，累遷太子舍人、尚書比部郎、撫軍主簿。

translations.literal: Before Xianzhi had capped his years, the province appointed him Retainer of the Council; he was recommended as Filial-and-Incorrupt and rose through Attendant of the Heir Apparent and Director of the Ministry of Justice Comparison Section to Registrar of the Pacification Army.
translations.idiomatic: Before he capped his years, the province appointed him Retainer of the Council; recommended as Filial-and-Incorrupt, he rose through Attendant of the Heir Apparent and Director of the Ministry of Justice Comparison Section to Registrar of the Pacification Army.

sentences.zh: 元徽中，爲建康令。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhui era he was Magistrate of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhui era he was magistrate of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 時有盜牛者，被主所認，盜者亦稱己牛，二家辭證等，前後令莫能決。

translations.literal: At the time there was a cattle thief whom the owner identified; the thief also claimed the ox was his—both households argued with equal force, and successive magistrates could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: A cattle thief was identified by the owner; the thief also claimed the ox was his—both argued equally, and successive magistrates could not decide.

sentences.zh: 憲之至，覆其狀，謂二家曰：「無爲多言，吾得之矣。

translations.literal: When Xianzhi arrived, he reviewed the case and told both households: "Say no more—I have got it."
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzhi arrived, he reviewed the case and told both households: "Say no more—I have got it."

sentences.zh: 」乃令解牛，任其所去，牛徑還本主宅，盜者始伏其辜。

translations.literal: He then had the ox untied and let it go where it would; the ox went straight to the true owner's house, and the thief at last confessed his crime.
translations.idiomatic: He had the ox untied and let it go where it would; the ox went straight to the true owner's house, and the thief at last confessed.

sentences.zh: 發姦擿伏，多如此類，時人號曰神明。

translations.literal: Exposing wrongdoing and unmasking the hidden—many cases were like this; people of the time called him divine in judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Exposing wrongdoing and unmasking the hidden—many cases were like this; people called him divine in judgment.

sentences.zh: 至於權要請託，長吏貪殘，據法直繩，無所阿縱。

translations.literal: As for powerful men's entreaties and long administrators' greed and cruelty, he held the law straight with the cord and never yielded to flattery.
translations.idiomatic: For powerful men's entreaties and greedy administrators, he held the law straight and never yielded to flattery.

sentences.zh: 性又清儉，強力爲政，甚得民和。

translations.literal: By nature he was also pure and frugal, governing with firm strength, and won the people's harmony exceedingly.
translations.idiomatic: Pure and frugal by nature, he governed with firm strength and won the people's harmony.

sentences.zh: 故京師飲酒者得醇旨，輒號爲「顧建康」，言醑清且美焉。

translations.literal: Hence those who drank in the capital, if they got rich flavor, would call it "Administrator Gu of Jiankang," saying the brew was clear and fine.
translations.idiomatic: Hence capital drinkers who got rich flavor called it "Administrator Gu of Jiankang," saying the brew was clear and fine.

sentences.zh: 遷車騎功曹、晉熙王友。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Registrar of the Chariots and Cavalry and Friend of the Prince of Jinxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Registrar of the Chariots and Cavalry and Friend of the Prince of Jinxi.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝執政，以爲驃騎錄事參軍，遷太尉西曹掾。

translations.literal: When Qi Gaozu held the government, he made him Recorder of the Rapid Cavalry and transferred him to Western Section Clerk of the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi Gaozu held the government, he made him Recorder of the Rapid Cavalry and transferred him to Western Section Clerk of the Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 齊臺建，爲中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Qi regime was established, he became Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi regime was established, he became Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝卽位，除衡陽內史。

translations.literal: When Qi Gaozu took the throne, he was appointed Administrator of Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi Gaozu took the throne, he was appointed administrator of Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 先是，郡境連歲疾疫，死者太半，棺木尤貴，悉裹以葦席，棄之路傍。

translations.literal: Before this, within the commandery plague had struck year after year and more than half had died; coffin wood was especially costly, and corpses were wrapped only in reed mats and cast beside the road.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, plague had struck year after year and more than half died; coffin wood was costly, and corpses were wrapped in reed mats and cast beside the road.

sentences.zh: 憲之下車，分告屬縣，求其親黨，悉令殯葬。

translations.literal: When Xianzhi took office, he sent word to the subordinate counties to seek kin and had them all buried properly.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzhi took office, he sent word to subordinate counties to seek kin and had them all buried properly.

sentences.zh: 其家人絕滅者，憲之爲出公祿，使綱紀營護之。

translations.literal: For families whose line was extinguished, Xianzhi paid from public salary and had the clerks arrange care.
translations.idiomatic: For families whose line was extinguished, Xianzhi paid from public salary and had clerks arrange care.

sentences.zh: 又土俗，山民有病，輒云先人爲禍，皆開塚剖棺，水洗枯骨，名爲除祟。

translations.literal: Again, by local custom when mountain folk fell ill they would say the ancestors were the harm, all opening tombs and coffins, washing dry bones—called "removing the curse."
translations.idiomatic: Again, by local custom when mountain folk fell ill they said ancestors were the harm, opening tombs and washing dry bones—called "removing the curse."

sentences.zh: 憲之曉喻，爲陳生死之別，事不相由，風俗遂改。

translations.literal: Xianzhi enlightened them, setting forth the distinction of life and death and that the affairs do not bear on one another—the custom was thus changed.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi enlightened them on life and death and that the affairs do not bear on one another—the custom changed.

sentences.zh: 時刺史王奐新至，唯衡陽獨無訟者，乃歎曰：「顧衡陽之化至矣。

translations.literal: At the time Inspector Wang Huan had newly arrived; only in Hengyang was there no litigation, and he sighed: "Administrator Gu of Hengyang's transformation has reached the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Wang Huan had newly arrived; only Hengyang had no litigation, and he sighed: "Administrator Gu of Hengyang's transformation has reached the utmost.

sentences.zh: 若九郡率然，吾將何事！」

translations.literal: If the nine commanderies were all like this, what would I have to do!"
translations.idiomatic: If the nine commanderies were all like this, what would I have to do!"

sentences.zh: 還爲太尉從事中郎。

translations.literal: He returned to serve as Retainer of the Masters of Affairs in the Grand Marshal's office.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as Retainer of the Masters of Affairs in the Grand Marshal's office.

sentences.zh: 出爲東中郎長史、行會稽郡事。

translations.literal: He went out as Chief Clerk of the Eastern General of the Gentlemen and Acting Administrator of Kuaiji commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Chief Clerk of the Eastern General of the Gentlemen and acting administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 山陰人呂文度有寵於齊武帝，於餘姚立邸，頗縱橫。

translations.literal: Lü Wendu of Shanyin had favor with Qi Wudi and established a lodge in Yuyao, behaving quite overbearingly.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Wendu of Shanyin had favor with Qi Wudi and established a lodge in Yuyao, behaving overbearingly.

sentences.zh: 憲之至郡，卽表除之。

translations.literal: When Xianzhi reached the commandery, he memorialized at once to remove it.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzhi reached the commandery, he memorialized at once to remove it.

sentences.zh: 文度後還葬母，郡縣爭赴弔，憲之不與相聞。

translations.literal: Wendu later returned to bury his mother; commandery and county competed to attend the mourning, but Xianzhi did not acknowledge it.
translations.idiomatic: Wendu later returned to bury his mother; commandery and county competed to attend mourning, but Xianzhi did not acknowledge it.

sentences.zh: 文度深銜之，卒不能傷也。

translations.literal: Wendu deeply resented this but in the end could not harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Wendu deeply resented this but in the end could not harm him.

sentences.zh: 遷南中郎巴陵王長史，加建威將軍、行婺州事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Prince of Baling in the Southern General of the Gentlemen, with additional title General Who Establishes Might and Acting Governor of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Prince of Baling in the Southern General of the Gentlemen, with additional title General Who Establishes Might and acting governor of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時司徒、竟陵王於宣城、臨成、定陵三縣界立屯，封山澤數百里，禁民樵采，憲之固陳不可，言甚切直。

translations.literal: At the time the Minister of Works, Prince of Jingling, established garrisons on the borders of Xuancheng, Lincheng, and Dingling counties, enclosing mountains and marshes for hundreds of li and forbidding the people firewood and gathering—Xianzhi firmly memorialized that this could not be, his words very blunt and direct.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Works, Prince of Jingling, enclosed mountains and marshes for hundreds of li and forbade firewood—Xianzhi firmly memorialized that this could not be, his words very blunt.

sentences.zh: 王答之曰：「非君無以聞此德音。

translations.literal: The Prince replied: "Without you I would not have heard this virtuous word."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince replied: "Without you I would not have heard this virtuous word."

sentences.zh: 」卽命無禁。

translations.literal: He at once ordered no prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: He at once ordered no prohibition.

sentences.zh: 遷給事黃門侍郎，兼尚書吏部郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant of the Yellow Gate and concurrently Director in the Ministry of Personnel Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Attendant of the Yellow Gate and concurrently Director in the Ministry of Personnel Section.

sentences.zh: 宋世，其祖覬之嘗爲吏部，於庭植嘉樹，謂人曰：「吾爲憲之種耳。

translations.literal: In Song times his grandfather Guan had once served in the Ministry of Personnel; in the courtyard he planted a fine tree and told people: "I am planting this for Xianzhi."
translations.idiomatic: In Song times his grandfather Guan had served in the Ministry of Personnel; in the courtyard he planted a fine tree and said: "I am planting this for Xianzhi."

sentences.zh: 」至是，憲之果爲此職。

translations.literal: At this time Xianzhi indeed held that office.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Xianzhi indeed held that office.

sentences.zh: 出爲征虜長史、行南兗州事，遭母憂。

translations.literal: He went out as Chief Clerk of the General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Acting Governor of Southern Yanzhou, and encountered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Chief Clerk of the General Who Punishes the Barbarians and acting governor of Southern Yanzhou, and encountered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，建武中，復除給事黃門侍郎，領步兵校尉。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, in the Jianwu era he was again appointed Attendant of the Yellow Gate and Colonel of the Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, in Jianwu he was again appointed Attendant of the Yellow Gate and Colonel of the Footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 未拜，仍遷太子中庶子，領吳邑中正。

translations.literal: Before he took the appointment he was transferred to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Rectifier of Wu district.
translations.idiomatic: Before he took the appointment he was transferred to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Rectifier of Wu district.

sentences.zh: 出爲寧朔將軍、臨川內史；

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Linchuan;
translations.idiomatic: He went out as General Who Pacifies the North and administrator of Linchuan;

sentences.zh: 未赴，改授輔國將軍、晉陵太守。

translations.literal: before he went, the appointment was changed to General Who Assists the State and Administrator of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: before he went, the appointment was changed to General Who Assists the State and administrator of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 頃之遇疾，陳解還鄉里。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he fell ill and petitioned to return to his home village.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he fell ill and petitioned to return to his home village.

sentences.zh: 永元初，徵爲廷尉，不拜，除豫章太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongyuan he was summoned as Minister of Justice but did not accept; he was appointed Administrator of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yongyuan he was summoned as Minister of Justice but did not accept; he was appointed administrator of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 有貞婦萬晞者，少孀居無子，事舅姑尤孝，父母欲奪而嫁之，誓死不許，憲之賜以束帛，表其節義。

translations.literal: There was a chaste widow, Wan Xi, who widowed young without sons and served her parents-in-law with utmost filiality; her parents wished to force her to remarry but she swore she would rather die—Xianzhi bestowed silk and memorialized her integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Chaste widow Wan Xi, widowed young without sons, served her parents-in-law with utmost filiality; her parents wished to force remarriage but she swore to die—Xianzhi bestowed silk and memorialized her integrity.

sentences.zh: 中興二年，義師平建康，高祖爲揚州牧，徵憲之爲別駕從事史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongxing, when the righteous army pacified Jiankang, Gaozu was Governor of Yangzhou and summoned Xianzhi as Retainer of the Separate Chariot.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongxing, when the righteous army pacified Jiankang, Gaozu was governor of Yangzhou and summoned Xianzhi as Retainer of the Separate Chariot.

sentences.zh: 比至，高祖已受禪，憲之風疾漸篤，固求還吳。

translations.literal: By the time he arrived, Gaozu had already received the abdication; Xianzhi's wind ailment grew severe and he firmly asked to return to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he arrived, Gaozu had already received the abdication; Xianzhi's wind ailment grew severe and he firmly asked to return to Wu.

sentences.zh: 天監二年，就家授太中大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjian, he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace at his home.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianjian, he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace at his home.

sentences.zh: 憲之雖累經宰郡，資無擔石。

translations.literal: Though Xianzhi had repeatedly governed commanderies, his assets did not amount to a dan of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xianzhi had repeatedly governed commanderies, his assets did not amount to a dan of grain.

sentences.zh: 及歸，環堵，不免饑寒。

translations.literal: When he returned, his ring of walls could not keep out hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, his ring of walls could not keep out hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 八年，卒於家，年七十四。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died at home, aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he died at home, aged seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 臨終爲制，以敕其子曰：

translations.literal: On his deathbed he made regulations and charged his sons, saying:
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he made regulations and charged his sons, saying:

sentences.zh: 夫出生入死，理均晝夜。

translations.literal: Birth and entering death, death and leaving life—reason treats them like day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Birth and entering death, death and leaving life—reason treats them like day and night.

sentences.zh: 生旣不知所從來，死亦安識所往。

translations.literal: While alive one does not know whence one came; in death how can one know whither one goes?
translations.idiomatic: While alive one does not know whence one came; in death how can one know whither one goes?

sentences.zh: 延陵所云「精氣上歸于天，骨肉下歸於地，魂氣則無所不之」，良有以也。

translations.literal: What Yanling said—"The refined breath returns to Heaven, flesh and bone return to earth, and the soul's breath goes everywhere"—has good grounds.
translations.idiomatic: What Yanling said—"The refined breath returns to Heaven, flesh and bone to earth, and the soul's breath goes everywhere"—has good grounds.

sentences.zh: 雖復茫昧難徵，要若非妄。

translations.literal: Though obscure and hard to verify, in essentials it is not vain.
translations.idiomatic: Though obscure and hard to verify, in essentials it is not vain.

sentences.zh: 百年之期，迅若馳隙。

translations.literal: A span of a hundred years is swift as a galloping gap.
translations.idiomatic: A span of a hundred years is swift as a galloping gap.

sentences.zh: 吾今豫爲終制，瞑目之後，念並遵行，勿違吾志也。

translations.literal: I now prepare these final regulations in advance; after my eyes close, think on them and follow them—do not go against my will.
translations.idiomatic: I now prepare these final regulations in advance; after my eyes close, follow them—do not go against my will.

sentences.zh: 莊周、澹臺，達生者也；

translations.literal: Zhuang Zhou and Tantai Mieming were men who had attained life;
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang Zhou and Tantai Mieming had attained life;

sentences.zh: 王孫、士安，矯俗者也。

translations.literal: Wang Sun and Shi An were men who had corrected vulgar custom.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sun and Shi An corrected vulgar custom.

sentences.zh: 吾進不及達，退無所矯。

translations.literal: In advance I do not reach attainment; in withdrawal I have nothing to correct.
translations.idiomatic: In advance I do not reach attainment; in withdrawal I have nothing to correct.

sentences.zh: 常謂中都之制，允理愜情。

translations.literal: I have always held that the mid-dynasty system accords with reason and satisfies feeling.
translations.idiomatic: I have always held that the mid-dynasty system accords with reason and satisfies feeling.

sentences.zh: 衣周於身，示不違禮；

translations.literal: Clothing sufficient for the body shows one does not violate ritual;
translations.idiomatic: Clothing sufficient for the body shows one does not violate ritual;

sentences.zh: 棺周於衣，足以蔽臭。

translations.literal: a coffin sufficient for the clothing is enough to cover stench.
translations.idiomatic: a coffin sufficient for the clothing is enough to cover stench.

sentences.zh: 入棺之物，一無所須。

translations.literal: What goes into the coffin—nothing is needed.
translations.idiomatic: What goes into the coffin—nothing is needed.

sentences.zh: 載以輴車，覆以粗布，爲使人勿惡也。

translations.literal: Carry on a bier-cart, cover with coarse cloth—so people will not be disgusted.
translations.idiomatic: Carry on a bier-cart, cover with coarse cloth—so people will not be disgusted.

sentences.zh: 漢明帝天子之尊，猶祭以杅水脯糗；

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Han, though honored as Son of Heaven, still sacrificed with ladle-water, dried meat, and parched grain;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Han, though Son of Heaven, still sacrificed with ladle-water, dried meat, and parched grain;

sentences.zh: 范史雲烈士之高，亦奠以寒水乾飯。

translations.literal: Fan Shiyun, lofty as a martyr, also offered cold water and dry rice.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Shiyun, lofty as a martyr, also offered cold water and dry rice.

sentences.zh: 況吾卑庸之人，其可不節衷也？

translations.literal: How much more for a man low and mediocre like me—can he not restrain his feelings?
translations.idiomatic: How much more for a low and mediocre man like me—can he not restrain his feelings?

sentences.zh: 喪易寧戚，自是親親之情；

translations.literal: Mourning is easy but dwelling in grief is hard—this is the affection of kin for kin;
translations.idiomatic: Mourning is easy but dwelling in grief is hard—this is kin affection;

sentences.zh: 禮奢寧儉，差可得由吾意。

translations.literal: ritual extravagant but dwelling in frugality is somewhat attainable according to my will.
translations.idiomatic: ritual extravagant but dwelling in frugality is somewhat attainable according to my will.

sentences.zh: 不須常施靈筵，可止設香燈，使致哀者有憑耳。

translations.literal: Do not constantly set out spirit mats; stop at lighting incense lamps, so those who would mourn have something to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Do not constantly set out spirit mats; stop at lighting incense lamps, so mourners have something to rely on.

sentences.zh: 朔望祥忌，可權安小床，暫設幾席，唯下素饌，勿用牲牢。

translations.literal: On the first and fifteenth and on mourning anniversaries, one may provisionally set a small couch and briefly place mats and seats, offering only plain food—do not use sacrificial animals.
translations.idiomatic: On the first and fifteenth and mourning anniversaries, provisionally set a small couch and briefly place mats, offering only plain food—do not use sacrificial animals.

sentences.zh: 蒸嘗之祠，貴賤罔替。

translations.literal: Seasonal sacrifices to ancestors—noble and base alike do not omit them.
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal sacrifices to ancestors—noble and base alike do not omit them.

sentences.zh: 備物難辦，多致疏怠。

translations.literal: Full provision is hard to prepare and often leads to neglect.
translations.idiomatic: Full provision is hard to prepare and often leads to neglect.

sentences.zh: 祠先人自有舊典，不可有闕。

translations.literal: Sacrificing to forebears has its old canon—it cannot be wanting.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificing to forebears has its old canon—it cannot be wanting.

sentences.zh: 自吾以下，祠止用蔬食時果，勿同於上世也。

translations.literal: From me downward, sacrifice only with vegetables, grain, seasonal fruit—do not be like the upper generations.
translations.idiomatic: From me downward, sacrifice only with vegetables, grain, and seasonal fruit—do not be like upper generations.

sentences.zh: 示令子孫，四時不忘其親耳。

translations.literal: Show the sons and grandsons so the four seasons do not forget their kin.
translations.idiomatic: Show sons and grandsons so the four seasons do not forget their kin.

sentences.zh: 孔子云：「雖菜羹瓜祭，必齊如也。

translations.literal: Confucius said: "Even with vegetable broth and melon sacrifice, one must be as if present."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: "Even with vegetable broth and melon sacrifice, one must be as if present."

sentences.zh: 」本貴誠敬，豈求備物哉？

translations.literal: The root values sincere reverence—how could one seek full provision?
translations.idiomatic: The root values sincere reverence—how could one seek full provision?

sentences.zh: 所著詩、賦、銘、贊幷《衡陽郡記》數十篇。

translations.literal: He authored poems, fu, inscriptions, eulogies, and several tens of chapters of the Record of Hengyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He authored poems, fu, inscriptions, eulogies, and several tens of chapters of the Record of Hengyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 陶季直

translations.literal: Tao Jizhi
translations.idiomatic: Tao Jizhi

sentences.zh: 陶季直，丹陽秣陵人也。

translations.literal: Tao Jizhi was a man of Moling in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Jizhi came from Moling in Danyang.

sentences.zh: 祖愍祖，宋廣州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Minzu was Song Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Minzu was Song inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 父景仁，中散大夫。

translations.literal: His father Jingren was Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jingren was palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 季直早慧，愍祖甚愛異之。

translations.literal: Minzu loved and favored him exceedingly for his early brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: Minzu loved and favored him exceedingly for his early brilliance.

sentences.zh: 愍祖嘗以四函銀列置於前，令諸孫各取，季直時甫四歲，獨不取。

translations.literal: Minzu once set four boxes of silver in a row before them and had the grandsons each take one; Jizhi was then only four and alone did not take.
translations.idiomatic: Minzu once set four boxes of silver before them and had the grandsons each take one; Jizhi was only four and alone did not take.

sentences.zh: 人問其故，季直曰：「若有賜，當先父伯，不應度及諸孫，是故不取。

translations.literal: When asked why, Jizhi said: "If there is a gift, it should go first to fathers and uncles—it should not pass to grandsons—therefore I do not take."
translations.idiomatic: When asked why, Jizhi said: "If there is a gift, it should go first to fathers and uncles—not to grandsons—therefore I do not take."

sentences.zh: 」愍祖益奇之。

translations.literal: Minzu admired him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Minzu admired him all the more.

sentences.zh: 五歲喪母，哀若成人。

translations.literal: At five he lost his mother and mourned as if an adult.
translations.idiomatic: At five he lost his mother and mourned as if an adult.

sentences.zh: 初，母未病，令於外染衣；

translations.literal: Earlier, before his mother fell ill, she had him dye clothes outside;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, before his mother fell ill, she had him dye clothes outside;

sentences.zh: 卒後，家人始贖，季直抱之號慟，聞者莫不酸感。

translations.literal: after her death the household at last redeemed them; Jizhi embraced them and wailed—hearers were all moved to sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: after her death the household at last redeemed them; Jizhi embraced them and wailed—hearers were all moved to sorrow.

sentences.zh: 及長，好學，淡於榮利。

translations.literal: When grown he loved learning and was indifferent to glory and profit.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he loved learning and was indifferent to glory and profit.

sentences.zh: 起家桂陽王國侍郎、北中郎鎮西行參軍，並不起，時人號曰「聘君」。

translations.literal: He began his career as Gentleman of the Kingdom of Guiyang and Army Aide on the Western Campaign of the Northern General of the Gentlemen, and did not take office—people of the time called him "the Invited Gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: He began as Gentleman of the Kingdom of Guiyang and Army Aide on the Western Campaign of the Northern General of the Gentlemen, and did not take office—people called him "the Invited Gentleman."

sentences.zh: 父憂服闋，尚書令劉秉領丹陽尹，引爲後軍主簿、領郡功曹。

translations.literal: When mourning for his father ended, Liu Bing, who was concurrently Administrator of Danyang, appointed him Chief Clerk of the Rear Army and concurrently Commandery Merit Officer.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning for his father ended, Liu Bing, concurrently administrator of Danyang, appointed him Chief Clerk of the Rear Army and concurrently Commandery Merit Officer.

sentences.zh: 出爲望蔡令，頃之以病免。

translations.literal: He went out as Magistrate of Wangcai; shortly afterward he was excused on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as magistrate of Wangcai; shortly afterward he was excused on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 時劉秉、袁粲以齊高帝權勢日盛，將圖之，秉素重季直，欲與之定策。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Bing and Yuan Can, because Qi Gaozu's power grew daily, were about to plot against him; Bing had always esteemed Jizhi and wished to settle strategy with him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Liu Bing and Yuan Can, because Qi Gaozu's power grew daily, were about to plot against him; Bing had always esteemed Jizhi and wished to settle strategy with him.

sentences.zh: 季直以袁、劉儒者，必致顛殞，固辭不赴。

translations.literal: Jizhi held that Yuan and Liu were Confucians and would surely come to ruin, and firmly declined to go.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi held that Yuan and Liu were Confucians and would surely come to ruin, and firmly declined to go.

sentences.zh: 俄而秉等伏誅。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Bing and the others were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Bing and the others were executed.

sentences.zh: 齊初，爲尚書比部郎，時褚淵爲尚書令，與季直素善，頻以爲司空司徒主簿，委以府事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qi he was Director of the Ministry of Justice Comparison Section; at the time Chu Yuan was Minister of Works and was on good terms with Jizhi, repeatedly making him Registrar of the Masters of Works and Minister of Works, entrusting him with bureau affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qi he was Director of the Ministry of Justice Comparison Section; Chu Yuan was Minister of Works and was on good terms with Jizhi, repeatedly making him Registrar of the Masters of Works and Minister of Works, entrusting him with bureau affairs.

sentences.zh: 淵卒，尚書令王儉以淵有至行，欲諡爲文孝公，季直請曰：「文孝是司馬道子諡，恐其人非具美，不如文簡。

translations.literal: When Yuan died, Minister of Works Wang Jian, because Yuan had utmost conduct, wished to posthumously title him Duke Wenxiao; Jizhi petitioned: "Wenxiao was Sima Daozi's posthumous title—I fear the man was not wholly good; better Wenjian."
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan died, Wang Jian wished to posthumously title him Duke Wenxiao; Jizhi petitioned: "Wenxiao was Sima Daozi's posthumous title—I fear the man was not wholly good; better Wenjian."

sentences.zh: 」儉從之。

translations.literal: Jian followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Jian followed this.

sentences.zh: 季直又請儉爲淵立碑，終始營護，甚有吏節，時人美之。

translations.literal: Jizhi also asked Jian to erect a stele for Yuan and saw to it from start to finish—very much the conduct of an official; people of the time praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi also asked Jian to erect a stele for Yuan and saw to it from start to finish—very much official conduct; people praised this.

sentences.zh: 遷太尉記室參軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Retainer of the Masters of Affairs in the Grand Marshal's office.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Retainer of the Masters of Affairs in the Grand Marshal's office.

sentences.zh: 出爲冠軍司馬、東莞太守，在郡號爲清和。

translations.literal: He went out as Army Aide to the Champion and Administrator of Dongguan; in the commandery he was known as pure and harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Army Aide to the Champion and administrator of Dongguan; in the commandery he was known as pure and harmonious.

sentences.zh: 還除散騎侍郎，領左衛司馬，轉鎮西諮議參軍。

translations.literal: On return he was appointed Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and concurrently Colonel of the Left Guard, then transferred to Army Adviser on the Western Campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was appointed Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Colonel of the Left Guard, then transferred to Army Adviser on the Western Campaign.

sentences.zh: 齊武帝崩，明帝作相，誅鋤異己，季直不能阿意，明帝頗忌之，乃出爲輔國長史、北海太守。

translations.literal: When Qi Wudi died, Mingdi became regent, executed and purged those unlike himself; Jizhi could not flatter his intent and Mingdi quite feared him, so he sent him out as Chief Clerk Who Assists the State and Administrator of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi Wudi died, Mingdi became regent and purged dissenters; Jizhi could not flatter him and Mingdi feared him, sending him out as Chief Clerk Who Assists the State and administrator of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 邊職上佐，素士罕爲之者。

translations.literal: Chief aide on a frontier post—plain scholars rarely held it.
translations.idiomatic: Chief aide on a frontier post—plain scholars rarely held it.

sentences.zh: 或勸季直造門致謝，明帝旣見，便留之，以爲驃騎諮議參軍，兼尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Some urged Jizhi to call at his gate and apologize; once Mingdi saw him he kept him, making him Army Adviser on the Rapid Cavalry and concurrently Director of the Left in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Jizhi to call at his gate and apologize; once Mingdi saw him he kept him, making him Army Adviser on the Rapid Cavalry and Director of the Left in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 仍遷建安太守，政尚清靜，百姓便之。

translations.literal: He was then transferred to Administrator of Jian'an; his government prized quiet purity and the people found it easy.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to administrator of Jian'an; his government prized quiet purity and the people found it easy.

sentences.zh: 還爲中書侍郎，遷遊擊將軍、兼廷尉。

translations.literal: On return he was Attendant of the Secretariat and transferred to General Who Strikes the Foe and concurrently Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was Attendant of the Secretariat and transferred to General Who Strikes the Foe and minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 梁臺建，遷給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Liang regime was established, he was transferred to Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang regime was established, he was transferred to Attendant of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 常稱仕至二千石，始願畢矣，無爲務人間之事，乃辭疾還鄉里。

translations.literal: He often said that serving to the rank of two-thousand-dan salary fulfilled his original wish, and he would not busy himself with worldly affairs—then he pleaded illness and returned to his home village.
translations.idiomatic: He often said that serving to two-thousand-dan salary fulfilled his original wish, and he would not busy himself with worldly affairs—then he pleaded illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 天監初，就家拜太中大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace at his home.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianjian he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace at his home.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「梁有天下，遂不見此人。

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "Liang has possessed the realm, yet I never saw this man."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said: "Liang has possessed the realm, yet I never saw this man."

sentences.zh: 」十年，卒於家，時年七十五。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he died at home, aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he died at home, aged seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 季直素清苦絕倫，又屏居十餘載，及死，家徒四壁，子孫無以殯斂，聞者莫不傷其志焉。

translations.literal: Jizhi was by nature pure and bitter beyond compare; he also lived in seclusion for more than ten years, and at death his house had only bare walls—sons and grandsons had no means for burial; hearers all grieved for his resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi was pure and bitter beyond compare; he lived in seclusion more than ten years, and at death his house had only bare walls—descendants had no means for burial; hearers grieved for his resolve.

sentences.zh: 蕭眎素

translations.literal: Xiao Shisu
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Shisu

sentences.zh: 蕭眎素，蘭陵人也。

translations.literal: Xiao Shisu was a man of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Shisu came from Lanling.

sentences.zh: 祖思話，宋征西儀同三司；

translations.literal: His grandfather Sihua was Song General of the West on Equal Terms with the Three Excellencies;
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sihua was Song General of the West on Equal Terms with the Three Excellencies;

sentences.zh: 父惠明，吳興太守；

translations.literal: his father Huiming was Administrator of Wuxing;
translations.idiomatic: his father Huiming was administrator of Wuxing;

sentences.zh: 皆有盛名。

translations.literal: both had great fame.
translations.idiomatic: both had great fame.

sentences.zh: 眎素早孤貧，爲叔父惠休所收卹。

translations.literal: Shisu was orphaned young and poor and was taken in and supported by his uncle Huixiu.
translations.idiomatic: Shisu was orphaned young and poor and was taken in by his uncle Huixiu.

sentences.zh: 起家爲齊司徒法曹行參軍，遷著作佐郎、太子舍人、尚書三公郎。

translations.literal: He began his career as Army Aide in the Law Section of the Qi Minister of Works, transferred to Assistant Gentleman of the Secretariat, Attendant of the Heir Apparent, and Director of the Three Excellencies Section in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Army Aide in the Law Section of the Qi Minister of Works, transferred to Assistant Gentleman of the Secretariat, Attendant of the Heir Apparent, and Director of the Three Excellencies Section.

sentences.zh: 永元末，爲太子洗馬。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongyuan he was Groom of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yongyuan he was Groom of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 梁臺建，高祖引爲中尉驃騎記室參軍。

translations.literal: When the Liang regime was established, Gaozu appointed him Retainer of the Masters of Affairs in the Rapid Cavalry and Central Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang regime was established, Gaozu appointed him Retainer of the Masters of Affairs in the Rapid Cavalry and Central Commandant.

sentences.zh: 天監初，爲臨川王友，復爲太子中舍人、丹陽尹丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian he was Friend of the Prince of Linchuan, then again Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Assistant to the Administrator of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianjian he was Friend of the Prince of Linchuan, then Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and assistant to the administrator of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 初拜，高祖賜錢八萬，眎素一朝散之親友。

translations.literal: On first taking office Gaozu bestowed eighty thousand cash; Shisu in one morning scattered it among kin and friends.
translations.idiomatic: On first taking office Gaozu bestowed eighty thousand cash; Shisu in one morning scattered it among kin and friends.

sentences.zh: 又遷司徒左西屬、南徐州治中。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Western Section Clerk of the Left in the Minister of Works and Concurrent Administrator of Southern Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again transferred to Western Section Clerk of the Left in the Minister of Works and concurrent administrator of Southern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 性靜退，少嗜欲，好學，能清言，榮利不關於口，喜怒不形於色。

translations.literal: By nature he was quiet and retiring, with few desires; he loved learning, could speak with pure refinement, and profit and glory did not touch his lips—joy and anger did not show on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Quiet and retiring by nature, with few desires; he loved learning, spoke with pure refinement, and profit and glory did not touch his lips—joy and anger did not show on his face.

sentences.zh: 在人間及居職，並任情通率，不自矜高，天然簡素，士人以此咸敬之。

translations.literal: Among people and in office he was always according to feeling, open and direct, never proud of himself; naturally plain and simple—scholar-gentry all honored him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Among people and in office he was open and direct, never proud; naturally plain and simple—scholars all honored him for this.

sentences.zh: 及在京口，便有終焉之志，乃於攝山築室。

translations.literal: When at Jingkou he already had the will to end his days there and built a house on Mt She.
translations.idiomatic: When at Jingkou he already had the will to end his days there and built a house on Mt She.

sentences.zh: 會徵爲中書侍郎，遂辭不就，因還山宅，獨居屏事，非親戚不得至其籬門。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Attendant of the Secretariat and then declined and did not go; he returned to his mountain dwelling, lived alone and screened affairs, and kin and friends could not reach his hedge gate.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as Attendant of the Secretariat, he declined; he returned to his mountain dwelling, lived alone, and kin and friends could not reach his hedge gate.

sentences.zh: 妻，太尉王儉女，久與別居，遂無子。

translations.literal: His wife was the daughter of Grand Marshal Wang Jian; long separated from him, in the end there were no sons.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was the daughter of Grand Marshal Wang Jian; long separated from him, in the end there were no sons.

sentences.zh: 八年，卒。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he died.

sentences.zh: 親故迹其事行，諡曰貞文先生。

translations.literal: Kin and friends traced his conduct and deeds and gave the posthumous title Recluse Zhenwen.
translations.idiomatic: Kin and friends traced his conduct and gave the posthumous title Recluse Zhenwen.

translations.literal: Commentary section marker in the source text.
translations.idiomatic: Marker denoting the historian's commentary section in the source text.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：顧憲之、陶季直，引年者也，蕭眎素則宦情鮮焉。

translations.literal: The historian says: Gu Xianzhi and Tao Jizhi cited age to withdraw; Xiao Shisu had little taste for office.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Gu Xianzhi and Tao Jizhi cited age to withdraw; Xiao Shisu had little taste for office.

sentences.zh: 比夫懷祿耽寵，婆娑人世，則殊間矣。

translations.literal: Compared with those who hug salary and cling to favor, lingering among men—how utterly different!
translations.idiomatic: Compared with those who hug salary and cling to favor, lingering among men—how utterly different!

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker in the source text.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial footnote marker in the source text.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七三年五月版《梁書》爲本校。

translations.literal: The full text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Liang (May 1973).
translations.idiomatic: The full text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Liang (May 1973).
